proposals.title: Bootstrap monorepo with npm workspaces, eliminating pnpm entirely
proposals.why_now: TASK-0001 has been rejected three consecutive times. All three rejections trace to a single environmental root cause: the authoritative validation environment resolves the pnpm command to /workspace/pnpm (a directory). Attempt-3 introduced a pnpm shim that faked frozen-lockfile installation success; this was correctly rejected (REVIEW-002) for weakening the installation gate. The only correct fix is to drop pnpm entirely: replace pnpm-workspace.yaml with a npm workspaces field in root package.json, replace pnpm-lock.yaml with package-lock.json, replace all pnpm invocations with npm ci and npm run. npm is unconditionally available wherever Node.js is installed and requires no corepack setup, no pnpm/action-setup, and no shim. Every substantive gate from the three prior attempts (determinism lint, dependency-boundary validation, tsconfig coverage for .ts/.tsx/.mts/.cts, negative fixture tests) must be carried forward. Nothing in the technical scope changes; only the package manager changes.

proposals.title: Write ADR-002 (hash function), ADR-004 (rounding enforcement), and ADR-009 (CanonicalEncoder)
proposals.why_now: §15 FASE-1 acceptance requires ADR-009 to be written and the CanonicalEncoder implemented before any state hash exists. ADR-002 requires the hash function specified bit-by-bit in an ADR before any rand() implementation. ADR-004's DEFINIR on the technical mechanism for rounding-mode enforcement must be resolved before the division helper can be correctly typed. All three ADRs are documentation-only changes to docs/decisions/ and can be authored immediately after IDEA-001 is accepted, before any numeric code exists. Implementing packages/core without these ADRs embeds unrecorded decisions that cannot be reversed without an encodingVersion bump and invalidation of all frozen reference StateHashes established in FASE-1.

proposals.title: Implement packages/core: branded types, positional RNG, division helpers, CanonicalEncoder
proposals.why_now: packages/core is the sole dependency of every other pure package. Without branded bigint types (Money, Quantity, Price, Rate) and safe-integer number types (Tick, noise indices), ADR-003 and ADR-004 have no enforcement mechanism and violations accumulate from the first file in any dependent package. Without rand() implementing ADR-002 bit-exactly, packages/world cannot be started. Without CanonicalEncoder implementing ADR-009, no StateHash can be computed and INV-01, INV-17, INV-22 have no foundation. This is the first implementation step after the monorepo and required ADRs are accepted.

proposals.title: Implement packages/world (price generator), packages/domain (ledger and market orders), packages/application (canonical tick loop and save)
proposals.why_now: These three packages compose the functional core required for FASE-1 acceptance. The price generator in packages/world delivers INV-02, described by the spec as the most important test in the project. The double-entry multi-commodity ledger in packages/domain delivers INV-04 through INV-07. The canonical ten-step tick loop in packages/application is an explicit FASE-1 acceptance criterion (§7 order is TRAVADO) and is the only layer legally allowed to compose world and domain without coupling them. Save structure per ADR-006 enables the CLI replay tool. None of these invariants can be fully verified in isolation. Note: the transcendental functions required for log-space price construction (Math.log, Math.exp) are prohibited in pure packages by §13. An additional ADR specifying a fixed-point or lookup-table implementation with bit-identical cross-platform results must be written before packages/world implementation begins.

proposals.title: Complete FASE-1: tools/replay, tools/bench, minimum Electron UI, platform installers, and CI matrix
proposals.why_now: FASE-1 acceptance requires tools/replay reporting the first divergent tick, tools/bench with calibration micro-benchmark and frozen ratio baseline in a versioned file, a minimum UI (lightweight-charts price chart, BRL balance, buy/sell market order buttons, pause and 1x time controls, permanent non-dismissable disclaimer from §20 in Portuguese), the simulation running in the dedicated worker, and installers for Windows and Linux. The performance baseline must be frozen in FASE-1 — deferring it means there is no regression reference for the rest of the project. §14.6 explicitly states the installer must exist in FASE-1 in minimum form to surface ABI and native-module failures before architecture is established. INV-19 requires cross-platform StateHash comparison between simulation-worker and CLI replay tool; INV-29 requires Electron security configuration verified programmatically in all modes.

repository_assessment.highest_priority_gap: TASK-0001 remains unaccepted after three attempts. The sole confirmed root cause across all three rejections is pnpm binary unavailability in the authoritative validation environment. The pnpm shim approach was rejected for falsely reporting installation success without installing or validating dependencies. Switching entirely to npm workspaces (npm ci, package-lock.json, no pnpm artifact of any kind) is the only path that eliminates the root cause without a shim. DEFINIR BLOCKER — transcendental functions for price generation: §5.1 constructs prices in log-space requiring Math.log and Math.exp; §13 prohibits both in pure packages. An ADR specifying a fixed-point or lookup-table implementation producing bit-identical cross-platform results must be written and accepted before packages/world can implement the price generator. This ADR is a prerequisite for IDEA-004 and is distinct from ADR-002, ADR-004, and ADR-009.

DEFINIR BLOCKER — octave parameters: the number of octaves, periods, and amplitudes for trendLayer and idiosyncraticNoise are DEFINIR per §5.1 and must be fixed in a versioned configuration file with an ADR before packages/world is implemented. Any post-implementation parameter change requires an encodingVersion bump and invalidates all reference StateHashes frozen by tools/bench.

DEFINIR BLOCKER — tools/* dependency edges: §14.5 defines the directed graph for packages/ and apps/ but not for tools/*. tools/replay and tools/bench must import from packages to fulfill FASE-1 acceptance. The allowed import edges for tools/ must be declared in a SPEC_BLOCKERS.md entry or ADR before those tools acquire cross-workspace imports.
